A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NewtonBench and contain 71 readable pages, including Appendices A–E. Full-text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 11 LLMs on 324 scientific discovery tasks, plus noise, code-assistance, judge-validation, memorization, and symbolic-regression experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical evaluations, including Table 2, the experimental analyses in Section 4, and the appendix results.

M1.justification: The counterfactual law construction, model-system interactions, optional code interpreter, and agent procedures in Sections 2–3 and Appendices A and C are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 108 shifted laws, 324 tasks, 12 physics domains, and three system-complexity settings. Noise scenarios and the NewtonBench and LSR-Transform DataBlind evaluations are also retained unchanged.

E2.justification: The same 11 LLMs participate in Table 2. The judge comparisons, DataBlind comparator sets, and PySR and LLM-SR comparisons in Appendix E.5 also retain identical membership.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics and settings remain identical, including temperature 0.4, up to 10 experimental rounds with 20 parameter sets per round, and the separate 5,000-sample fidelity evaluation. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The noise and code-budget analyses, physical-plausibility breakdown, judge robustness and few-shot analyses, DataBlind tests, and Appendix D case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify four independent runs, report standard deviations in Table 2, and describe plot error bars as 95% confidence intervals in Appendix A.1. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are retained, including the appendix results. For example, Table 2 reports GPT-5 symbolic accuracy of 75.9% without code assistance and 73.3% with assistance in both versions.

T1.justification: The equation and model definitions, expression-tree algorithm, mathematical metrics, and Appendix E.2 solvability assumptions A0–A4 and proofs are unchanged. The Section 2 typo correction does not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about counterfactual, interactive discovery evaluation, fragility under complexity and noise, and the differing effects of code assistance.

C2.justification: The exploration–exploitation interpretation and correlational qualification remain unchanged, as do the physical-plausibility caveats and Appendix E.6 limitation concerning predefined experimental environments.

D1.justification: Page 11 changes code and data from 'will be publicly released' to 'are publicly released' and changes the documentation location from 'both Appendix and Supplementary Materials' to 'Appendix'. The repository link and technical appendices are unchanged. Actual external availability is not verified by the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: Related work, research positioning, and the cited-work set are unchanged. References move across page breaks following the added acknowledgments; none are added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 adds funding acknowledgments, replaces the NewtonBench running header with an ICLR 2026 publication statement, corrects 'equatons' to 'equations', and edits the reproducibility paragraph. The scientific narrative and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The running headers change, and the acknowledgments shift the ethics, reproducibility, and reference blocks on pages 11–15. All figures and tables retain their content, styling, and placement.

improvement.justification: The research content and supporting evidence, including all appendices, are unchanged. v3 adds acknowledgments, minor editorial polish, and an updated release statement while retaining the same repository link and technical documentation. These administrative and disclosure edits do not materially improve or impair the paper's overall quality.
